extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners at KIPO, Korean patent attorneys and applicants (practitioners interacting with Korean patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Official examination guidelines under the Korean Patent Act covering domestic priority, non-prejudicial disclosure, divisional/converted applications, applications by entitled persons, international (PCT) applications, and the notice-of-rejection procedure. Intended to direct examiners' actions and inform applicants of procedural and substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim — combination of earlier application subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: For a domestic priority claim based on 2 or more earlier applications, when the invention of the priority claim is a combination of technical subject-matter separately stated in 2 or more first specification of earlier applications, or a combination of new technical subject-matter and those separately stated in 2 or more first specification of earlier applications, the invention of the priority claim shall be treated as an 'invention which is not stated in the first specification of earlier application'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such combination as not entitled to the earlier filing date for priority purposes; examiner must apply the rules for inventions not stated in earlier first specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity when earlier application itself claims priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When the earlier application which forms a basis of the domestic priority claim claims priority based on another application filed beforehand, the effect of the priority claim shall not be recognized for the invention which is stated in both the first specification of the earlier application and another priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall not conduct examination as of the earlier application's filing date for overlapping subject-matter; if prior art discovered prevents retroactive application, examiner must specify reason for non-retroactive application in the notice of grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when earlier application and priority-app are identical and earlier app considered withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventions stated in the first specification or drawings attached to the application with domestic priority claim and those in the first specification of the earlier application are identical, the earlier application (deemed withdrawn when one year and three months has lapsed from the filing date) is regarded to be laid open at the time when the application with the priority claim is laid open or published in the patent gazette in applying Article 29(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of lay-open timing and withdrawal timing (1 year 3 months) when assessing prior art and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier application deemed withdrawn after 1 year 3 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The earlier application that served as a basis of the domestic priority claim shall be regarded withdrawn when one year and three months has lapsed from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check withdrawal status and defer or resume examination accordingly (see related deferral rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination upon domestic priority claim discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner discovers that the application under his examination is based on the domestic priority claim, he/she shall defer further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the domestic priority claim is invalidated due to deficiency in formalities, the examiner shall resume examination on the suspended application and consider potential conflicts with other applications (Article 29(3), Article 36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant deferred until earlier application considered withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to grant a patent on the domestic priority claim shall be deferred till the earlier application is considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preferential examination is carried out on the application with domestic priority claim, notify the applicant that grant will be deferred until earlier application is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure — six-month filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application with the statement under Article 30(2) is filed, the examiner shall examine whether the application is filed within six months from the prescribed publication date stated in the application; if filed after the due period, request amendments and invalidate the claim if deficiency not cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely claim for non-prejudicial disclosure is considered not overcome; enforce strict six-month deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure — proof when disclosure by right-holder
rubrics_metrics.description: When non-prejudicial disclosure is claimed because publication was made by a person with a right to obtain a patent, the examiner shall examine whether (i) that person has a right to obtain a patent upon the public disclosure, (ii) whether the purport is stated in the application, and (iii) whether evidential documents of the public disclosure are submitted within thirty days from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies discovered, request amendments and invalidate the claim if not cured; pay special attention where discloser ≠ applicant, incorrect type/date, insufficient evidence, or evidential docs submitted without stating purport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure — multiple disclosures handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple public disclosures, the claimant shall state the purport individually by each public disclosure with corresponding evidential documents; if disclosures are closely connected, evidential documents for subsequent disclosures may not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: exhibition display and separate market sales generally require separate evidential documents; if market sales are closely connected under exhibition contract, documents for market sales can be exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure — per-claim legitimacy assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple claims for non-prejudicial disclosure, the legitimacy of the claim shall be judged by each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess every claim separately for legitimacy and effect on novelty/inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recognized non-prejudicial disclosure on novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claim for non-prejudicial disclosure is recognized as legitimate, novelty and inventive step are judged as if the concerned invention having publicly known deems not to be known publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat recognized non-prejudicial disclosures as if the public disclosure did not defeat novelty/inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a divisional/converted application
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can file a divisional or converted application is an applicant of its original application; where applicants are not identical, an examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition and then return the concerned application. Scope of applicant-correction amendments is limited to obvious error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide identity of applicants as of the time the divisional/converted application is submitted; name changes may be legitimate if effective on filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for filing divisional and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be filed only during the period designated for amendment of specification/drawings or during the period designated for an appeal against decision to reject; conversion shall be made within thirty days from the date applicant initially receives a certified copy of decision to reject (extensions possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional shall not be filed after a request for appeal is filed; exceptions where trial withdrawn and appeal period not expired may permit divisional filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing after statutory period — petition/return procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional or converted application is filed after the statutory period expiry, an examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition to an applicant and then return the application pursuant to Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow petition/return procedures; do not accept late filings without statutory justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: No division/conversion from invalidated/withdrawn/or already-registered original application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or confirmed for decision of rejection, division or conversion shall not be made based on the application. Also, a converted application cannot be filed after registration of establishment of patent right for the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide petition/return if such filings are attempted; only legitimately-filed division/conversion before closure are processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional content must be within original disclosure scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters described in the specification or drawings of divisional applications shall be within the scope of matters described in the specification or drawings of the original application as of the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If division/conversion exceeds scope, treat depending on filing date of original application (see pre-/post-30 Sep 2006 rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-2006 handling of inadmissible division/conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original application was filed before Sept 30, 2006, an examiner shall deliver a warning notice for inadmissible division (conversion); if applicant's arguments fail, deliver a notice for inadmissible division (conversion) and conduct examination as of filing date of divisional (converted) application, not retroactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm admissibility of conversion/division before notifying other grounds where possible; if scope violation cured during examination, examination may be conducted retroactively to original filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-2006 handling of scope-violation division/conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original application filed after Oct 1, 2006, an examiner shall deliver a written notice of the ground for rejection by reason of scope (division or conversion) violation; if arguments/amendments fail to cure scope violation, examiner shall make a decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other rejection reasons exist, include them in the same written notice of rejection grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing scope violation permits retroactive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a violation of division (conversion) scope is legitimately cured during an examination stage, the examination shall be conducted retroactively on the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor amendment history to determine whether retroactivity should apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional identical to original claims — Article 36(2) consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional application is made legally and a claimed invention of the divisional application is identical to a claimed invention of the original application after the division, the applications shall be subject to Article 36(2); amendments of the original application are required and shall be made at the time of filing date of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate amendments are made to the original application to avoid double-patenting conflicts per Article 36(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain divisional rule (A→B→C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original application A is divided into B and B into C, Application C is regarded legal and deemed filed at the time of filing of A, provided B meets all requirements for division as to A and C meets all requirements as to B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply same treatment to converted applications; verify each divisional in the chain meets division requirements relative to its parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for application by a person entitled (lawful holder)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application to be recognized as by a lawful holder, these requirements shall be met: (①) unentitled person's application filed earlier than by lawful holder; (②) unentitled person's application is rejected or invalidated due to illegitimacy of applicant; (③) lawful holder files within thirty days from date of rejection or invalidation confirmation (with extra 'within two years from publication of registration' requirement in some invalidation cases); (④) scope of claimed invention in lawful holder's application falls within invention scope in application by unentitled person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lawful-holder form used, examiner shall study legitimacy before other grounds; if doubts on requirements ①, ③, ④, deliver notice that filing date shall not be retroactive; if ② not satisfied, defer examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive filing-date effect for lawful-holder applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is recognized as legitimate by the lawful holder pursuant to Articles 34, 35, it is deemed to have been filed at the date when the unentitled person filed; thus judgments of patent requirements, period calculations, and related rules are determined as of that earlier date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party intervening filings between the unentitled filing and lawful-holder filing do not invalidate the lawful-holder's retroactive claim; third-party applications may be rejected based on lawful-holder's retroactive date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request-for-examination timing for lawful-holder applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination for an application by the lawful holder after five years from the filing date of the unentitled person's application is deemed valid as long as the lawful-holder application and the request for examination are filed simultaneously (or on the same date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure simultaneous filing of application and request for examination in these delayed cases to maintain validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for lawful-holder retroactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of invention in an application by the lawful holder is limited to claimed inventions as well as those disclosed in the specification or drawings of the application by the unentitled person; inventions beyond that scope do not receive retroactive filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lawful-holder application includes inventions beyond the unentitled person's disclosure, those inventions are examined with the actual (non-retroactive) filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) application treated as ordinary domestic application on international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An International Patent Application (PCT) is treated as an ordinary patent application filed on the international filing date; description, claims, and drawings submitted at international application are considered legitimate under Article 42(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translation must be submitted per Article 201 or the international application filed in foreign language is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT priority vs domestic priority distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application enters domestic phase with Korean translation submitted, claiming priority under the PCT, this priority claim is treated as the priority claim under the Treaty. If the application serving as basis of the priority claim is a Korean application or an international app where Korea is the only designated State, the priority claim is considered domestic priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a priority claim is Treaty-based or domestic based on identity/nature of the earlier application and designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and lay-open timing for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application becomes 'another application' referred to in Article 29(3), the application is considered to be laid open at the time of international publication; scope of inventions limited to those described in the international application as of the international filing date and its translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing novelty/inventive step, limit cited content to what was present at international filing date and in the translation submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority based on international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an earlier application that serves as domestic priority claim is an international application, inventions commonly stated in both an application with the domestic priority claim and the earlier international application (limited to description, claims or drawings submitted at international filing date) are considered to have been filed at the international filing date of the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply retroactive filing date to commonly stated subject-matter only within the international application's filing-date materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean translation of PCT amendments — self-amendment treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Korean translation of written amendment regarding description or claims under PCT Articles 19 or 34 is submitted within the reference date, an examiner proceeds considering an international application to have been self-amended under Article 47 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept translations of PCT amendments submitted timely as part of domestic file history for amendment scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible amendments for international applications filed in foreign language
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of amendments to the specification of an international application filed in a foreign language is limited to the description, claims, or drawings (limited to explanatory parts in drawings) of its translation, or drawings (except explanatory parts) of the international application as of the international filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit amendments that introduce matter outside the translated materials or the original international application drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may request ISR/IPER documents for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request an applicant of an international application to submit copies of documents cited in the International Search Report or International Preliminary Examination Report; Commissioner of KIPO may request submission within designated period if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ISR/IPER citations as useful prosecution aids; request copies when necessary for examination completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grounds for rejection requirement (Article 62)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before decision to reject an application, the examiner should notify an applicant of the grounds for rejection and give opportunity to submit a written argument within a designated period (purpose: prevent errors and provide opportunity under First-to-File).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Article 62 procedural protections; notify applicant and provide the opportunity even where grounds are clear to avoid harsh immediate rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated grounds for rejection (list of bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds for rejection include: (①) claimed invention not patentable pursuant to Articles 25, 29, 32, 36(1),(3) or 44; ② no persons entitled to obtain a patent or subject to proviso of Article 33(1); ③ violation of treaty clauses; ④ requirements in Article 42(3),(4),(8) or Article 45 not satisfied; ⑤ amendment out of scope per Article 47(2); ⑥ divisional filed out of scope per Article 52(1); ⑦ converted application filed out of scope per Article 53(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing grounds, cite the specific statutory provisions and state grounds claim-by-claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for submission of response to notice of grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for submission shall be within two months regardless of residency; the period may add additional time required for tests or evaluations when acknowledged. (Note: period designated by Commissioner for amendment request under Article 46 is one month.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply two-month default response period; extend as needed for justified test time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective notification of grounds — general rule and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except special cases, all grounds for rejection discovered during examination shall be notified collectively. Exceptions: (i) where contents cannot be comprehended due to lack of clarity, notify only Article 42(3),(4) without prior art search (unless clarity insufficiency is insignificant); (ii) where certain grounds like newly added matter or non-invention are clear, notify those grounds without judging novelty/inventive step; (iii) lack of unity under Article 45 — examiner may examine inventions within a group and notify discovered grounds along with lack-of-unity rejection; examiner may notify lack of unity before other patentability requirements when efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collective notification to protect applicant's amendment interests, but apply exceptions where appropriate for efficiency or when other grounds are not examinable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of notice of grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying grounds for rejection, the examiner shall stipulate the relevant provisions and indicate grounds on a claim-by-claim basis; statements should be definite, concise, and normal sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific: (i) for inventive step cite minimum necessary documents and specify parts relied upon; (ii) where alleging public knowledge/work, state specific facts; (iii) for detailed-description deficiency specify deficient parts and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may suggest division/conversion in notice (non-binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: If helpful for applicant response and for accurate/expeditious examination, an examiner may suggest a division or conversion of an application in the notice of rejection grounds, but must stipulate the suggestion has no legal effects and the decision is the applicant's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat suggestions as advisory only; do not treat suggestion as part of official decision-making unless applicant elects to pursue it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of written notice errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a written notice of rejection grounds contains errors in writing, an examiner shall issue a correct notice regardless of whether an applicant submits an argument, except where (i) applicant is deemed to submit arguments based on correct understanding of errors, or (ii) applicant does not submit any arguments and errors are trivial misspellings not influential to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Err on the side of correcting substantive mistakes in notices; trivial typos may be excused if they don't impact applicant's response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling self-evident errors in description
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description contains a self-evident error in writing, an examiner shall notify the error as 'Considerations' if there are other grounds for rejection; if no other grounds, communicate by telephone and may advise applicant to self-amend or amend ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document advice/guidance in 'Applicant/Attorney Personal Interview' in the Examination Report; treat self-evident errors informally when no other rejections exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection without additional notice when grounds previously notified persist
rubrics_metrics.description: If previously-notified grounds remain after considering amendments, examiner should make a decision of rejection without an additional notice provided the ground in the rejection decision primarily coincides with previously-notified grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary coincidence is assessed practically (whether applicant had opportunity to respond). Where different statutory provisions apply, different cited documents are used, newly-established claims arise, or inventions newly become identical to previously-unnotified claims, issue notice again rather than proceed straight to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where prior-notice coincidence is not admitted (new notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples requiring new notice: (1) different provisions of Act/Rules applied to same claim; (2) different type or number of cited inventions denying novelty/inventive step; (3) ground lies in a newly-established claim by amendment; (4) invention becomes identical with a claim in which grounds had never been notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases, issue fresh notice of grounds for rejection rather than treating them as the same prior ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final notice of grounds for rejection — when to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may issue a non-final notice regardless of self-amendments if it is the first notice since start of examination, when identifying a ground in amendment confirmation not yet amended, or when grounds are not necessitated by amendments made in response to prior notice. Also when grounds established due to reasons other than amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final notices preserve applicant opportunity to amend; examples provided (claim changed insignificantly and prior art found) illustrate non-final issuance even after amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final notice of grounds for rejection — definition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A final notice is issued where the ground for rejection incurs from amendments corresponding to a previously-issued notice of grounds for rejection; amendments according to prior notice are prerequisite. Examples: (1) amendments add new matter or exceed permissible division/conversion scope; (2) claim amendments cause novelty or inventive step issues; (3) newly generated/substantially changed claims contain novelty/inventive step grounds; (4) reexamination after amendment reveals novelty/inventive step grounds that were previously inexamnable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final notices are narrower in amendment scope allowed to applicant; see selection rules for when to issue final vs non-final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rule between final and non-final notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner discovers the ground after reexamination, issue non-final notice unless all grounds fall under final notice criteria. If uncertain between the two types, issue non-final to avoid unreasonably limiting applicant's opportunity for amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to non-final if doubt exists to preserve applicant rights; only use final when prerequisites clearly met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on a claim-by-claim basis — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner examines an application to ensure compliance with patentability requirements on a claim-by-claim basis; even a single ground for rejection in the application prevents grant based on that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed claim-by-claim in presenting grounds for rejection and in analysis of prior art, novelty, inventive step, support, etc.; see '5.4 Examination Method by Each Claim' for details.
